payload.text: Fidelity evidence names an artifact a later reader can OBTAIN or REBUILD, or states plainly that it cannot and why. MEASURED 2026-09-09 by snorkeltoast and verified by vc: the 45h reel is entirely untracked -- 23 files, 15 MB, ZERO under git, and matched by no ignore rule, so it is unadded rather than deliberately excluded, in a parent directory that does carry 3 tracked files. FLOORS.md therefore cites sha256 daaa503ad7db for a build existing on one machine: the hash identifies the artifact precisely and makes it no easier to obtain, and the sha's only function was to let a reader verify. A PROVENANCE LINE THAT CANNOT BE FOLLOWED IS MOST OF A PROVENANCE LINE MISSING. THE 15 MB IS NOT ONE DECISION AND MUST NOT BE PUT TO hv AS ONE, which is vc's measurement: showreel.yaml is 8 KB in 1 file and is the reel's DESCRIPTION; assets/ is 5.7 MB in 16 files and is the source; _out/ is 9.2 MB in 3 files and is DERIVED, regenerable from the other two and never a thing to commit; plus .raster/ at 256 KB of intermediate cache and a 12 KB .DS_Store, both of which want an ignore rule rather than a decision. So the repository question is 5.7 MB of source images, the config costs nothing, and 9.2 MB of the total is an answer nobody should store. AND OBTAINABLE IS NOT THE SAME AS BYTE-REPRODUCIBLE -- THOUGH THE MEASURED CAUSE IS STRONGER THAN THIS ROW ORIGINALLY GAVE, AND THE CONCLUSION IS UNCHANGED. This row said a rebuild differs because the encoder's bytes depend on its VERSION. MEASURED 2026-09-09 by snorkeltoast, five ways: the TTF-to-WOFF2 conversion in the reference's font_face() is NONDETERMINISTIC ACROSS PROCESSES AT FIXED VERSION -- same font, same interpreter, same fontTools 4.61.1, same brotli 1.2.0, five separate processes giving two distinct shas, and six probes spanning 36896 to 37028 bytes. Stable WITHIN a process, unstable across them, which is why nobody caught it: nothing ever converted the same font twice in one run. PYTHONHASHSEED pinned to 0 leaves 3 of 5 fonts still differing, so it is not hash randomisation. So version drift was a true cause and not the operative one, and committing config and assets makes the reel REBUILDABLE, not identical, because the build contained a fresh random draw every time. **THE SHA WAS NEVER A RECIPE, ONLY A NAME** -- snorkeltoast's distinction, and it is the correction to vc, who reasoned from *the conversion is nondeterministic* to *the sha is not a stable identifier* and skipped the step that the nondeterminism is in the PRODUCTION of the file and never in the HASHING of it. A sha is always a faithful function of bytes. daaa503ad7db identifies the bytes that were captured, exactly as before, and FLOORS.md's floors remain measurements of one specific artifact. What is newly known to be false is a claim this contract never made: that rebuilding 008's config would yield 008. **AND THE FIX MAKES IT REPRODUCIBLE FOR THE FIRST TIME** -- committing the WOFF2 bytes removes the only nondeterministic step, and two full builds of the whole reel now come out BYTE-IDENTICAL at ae90d9e88b0fcdba, where five builds of one font previously gave two results. So this clause is now true only of builds made BEFORE that change -- which is the same fact that makes WP-02 necessary for the Rust port at all. A rebuild that yields a different sha is not evidence of a defect and not evidence of its absence; only the harness can tell those apart. So the sha identifies, the inputs make it rebuildable, and the harness makes a rebuild gradeable, and provenance is followable only with all three. DISCHARGED, AND NOT BY TRACKING ANYTHING. hv RULED 2026-09-09 that the reel's inputs stay in Dropbox: the reel lives in a Dropbox worktree rather than a git one, its inputs can be arbitrarily large, and Utilz itself is fully tracked, which is what the hoist actually depends on. THIS ROW IS NOT AN ACTION ITEM AND MUST NOT READ AS ONE -- snorkeltoast's point when the ruling landed. The limit is permanent and TRUE: a later reader cannot resolve sha256 daaa503ad7db, and nobody intends to change that. What the row still requires is the honest half -- FLOORS.md states at the point the sha is read what a reader can and cannot do with it, which it does. The three-legged reading holds and is now the whole of it: the sha identifies, the inputs are unobtainable so nothing makes the reel rebuildable by a third party, and the harness is what makes any rebuild gradeable for whoever does hold the inputs.
